title: fix: serve catalog health from an hourly materialized view
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Every `/models` list ran two raw-event scans: the last 50 community requests over 7 days, and 24h official health. Each Cloudflare location cached them for only 60s, so a few hundred locations meant tens of thousands of scans a day. Over the last 3 days these two feeds used about 6 CPU-hours a day in prod.

- Adds `model_health_hourly`, a materialized view holding final 2xx/5xx counts plus the latest 50 requests per model and hour, with an 8-day TTL and a backfill capped at 8 days
- `model_catalog_health` now merges hourly state (at most 168 rows per model) instead of scanning 7 days of events
- Adds `model_health_24h` for official models and agents; gen points `fetchModelHealthRows` at it in place of `model_route_health?minutes=1440`
- `model_route_health` stays as it is for `/models/status` and the monitor

Parity against prod events (read-only SQL):

| Feed | Matches current output |
|---|---|
| community last 50 | 491 / 491 models identical |
| official 24h status | 499 / 501; 2 differ by one request in the extra partial hour |

**Deploy order:** Tinybird prod first, then gen. Gen reaching prod first would show "unknown" health on official models until Tinybird lands.

Replaces #16497 (KV cache, which stampedes at expiry).

gist.headline: Health checks stop digging
gist.blurb: The model catalog gets tidy hourly health snapshots instead of repeatedly excavating raw events. Less digging, same useful signals.
gist.summary: The /models health feeds use an hourly materialized view with an 8-day TTL, merging at most 168 hourly rows per model for community health and using model_health_24h for official models and agents.
gist.impact: Model listings retain last-50 community and 24-hour official health signals without repeated seven-day raw-event scans.
